Q3.why: Hyperparameters are already known; listing them is a table.

Q4.why: Baseline settings must be gathered from configs or papers, but nothing new is run.

Q5.why: Posting a repository link costs a few minutes and cannot change results.

Q6.why: Describing the search already done is a paragraph; it only exposes weak tuning.

Q7.why: Needs held-out seeds, tasks or data, often new runs, and results often drop.

Q8.why: A test on existing runs is cheap but often shows the gain is not significant.

X2.why: Computing std or intervals from existing seeds is easy but can reveal overlap.

X3.why: Reporting all runs instead of the best needs full results and often shrinks gains.

X4.why: Tuning baselines equally means many new runs and often erases the claimed advantage.

X7.why: Stating hours or GPU-hours from logs is a sentence.

Y1.why: Defining the metric and measurement point is a sentence.

Y5.why: Naming the baseline code bases is a sentence or citation.

Y7.why: Stating environment versions is a sentence.

Y8.why: Requires new evaluations or training under shifted conditions, where methods often fail.

Y9.why: A hyperparameter sweep needs several new runs and may reveal fragility.

Y10.why: Exporting a requirements file with versions is trivial.

Y12.why: Running rliable on existing scores is easy but IQM intervals often widen and weaken claims.
